title: First login: Classic or Enhanced Experience Preset
claim: At first login you pick an Experience Preset: Enhanced turns on quest markers and objective areas, one-bag, transmog, HD models and strafe keys; Classic turns them off. Each can be changed later in Options.
detail: Blizzard's New Player's Starter Guide (Oct 28): the preset screen appears once, at first login, before the ruleset choice, and does not come back. Classic: Standard Definition models, quest points of interest and objective blobs off, One-bag off, transmog off, camera-turning default keybinds, Classic screen UI layout. Enhanced: High Definition models, quest points of interest and objective blobs on, One-bag on, transmog on, strafe default keybinds, centralized UI layout. Blizzard recommends Enhanced if unsure. All six settings can be changed under Game Menu > Options; HD or SD models are also chosen per character (appearance only, changeable at a Barbershop). For leveling speed the quest objective areas on the map are the setting that matters; a player who wants the Classic look can pick Classic and turn only that option on.

title: Grouping and guilds only within one ruleset and faction
claim: Characters can group, join guilds, run dungeons and raid only with players on the same ruleset and faction, so agree on both with friends before creating characters.
detail: Blizzard's New Player's Starter Guide (Oct 28), Rulesets section. Rulesets at launch: Normal, PvP, Roleplay and Roleplay-PvP; Hardcore comes later with no date. timesaver.gg's launch checklist (updated Oct 30, citing Blizzard news) adds that PvP rulesets allow only one faction per account and that the language setting is account-wide with a 24-hour cooldown; those two points are not in the Blizzard text read on Nov 2, so treat them as reported. US forum thread 2392155 ('Faction lock for both PVP and RP-PvP') discusses the faction lock. Check each new character's ruleset (see 20261031-ruleset-listing-bug).

title: Free 6-slot bag from a starting-zone quest
claim: Every starting zone has a level 1-4 quest with a guaranteed 6-slot bag, such as Book Return in Elwynn Forest, Sticks And Bones in Tirisfal Glades and Carry Your Weight in Durotar.
detail: Method (Oct 28, beta data that may change). Human: Book Bag from Book Return (end of the elite Nibbled-On Book chain, Marshal Dughan, level 1). Dwarf/Gnome: Canvas Latchbag from Grund And Gozwin (Grund Drokda, Dun Morogh, 4). Night Elf: Soft Saber Sack from Soft Saber Pelts (Aldia, Teldrassil, 4). Skyborne: Simple Leather Satchel from The Problem With Prideclaws (Indari Sunseam, Zephras Isle, 4). Undead: Collecting Basket from Sticks And Bones (Deathguard Bartholomew, Tirisfal Glades, 4). Orc/Troll: Handmade Leather Bag from Carry Your Weight (Furl Scornbrow, Durotar, 4). Tauren: Scorched Leather Pouch from Grace of An'she and Mu'sha (Seer Graytongue, Mulgore, 1). Small colored 6-slot pouches also drop from starting-zone mobs at about 0.5-1%. Vendor bags: Small Brown Pouch 6 slots 5 s, Brown Leather Satchel 8 slots 25 s, Heavy Brown Bag 10 slots 2 g, Huge Brown Sack 12 slots 10 g.

title: Free 8-slot quest bags at levels 9-14
claim: Free 8-slot bags at levels 9-14: Parts and Pieces in The Barrens (Scuffed Shipping Crate), Poor Old Blanchy in Westfall (Feed Pouch, now 8 slots) and the Buzzbox chain from Auberdine (Wizbang's Gunnysack).
detail: Method (Oct 28, beta data). Parts and Pieces is a new level 14 Barrens quest, available from level 9: bring 5 Handfuls of Complicated Parts from the upper pirate camp south of Ratchet to Wrenix the Wretched (63.1, 36.4) in Ratchet; both factions can take it (Alliance would reach Ratchet via Booty Bay near level 30). Poor Old Blanchy (level 14, from 9): 8 Handfuls of Oats to Verna Furlbrow (60, 19.4); the Feed Pouch is 8 slots in Forever (4 in Classic). Wizbang's Gunnysack (8 slots, was 6) ends the Buzzbox chain at Buzzbox 525, from level 7. Ten-slot reward choices: Deviate Hides (Wailing Caverns, from 13) and Vyrin's Revenge (Loch Modan, Alliance, from 15).

title: Separate Reagent Bag slot; first reagent bags at skill 5/30
claim: Forever adds a separate Reagent Bag slot next to the four bag slots; Tailors make a 6-slot Linen Reagent Bag at skill 5 and Leatherworkers a 6-slot Light Leather Reagent Bag at skill 30.
detail: Method (Oct 28, beta data). Linen Reagent Bag: pattern about 1 s 50 c from Tailoring Supplies vendors, 6 Bolts of Linen Cloth and 6 Coarse Thread. Woolen Reagent Bag: 8 slots, skill 70, pattern 2 s 50 c, 3 Bolts of Woolen Cloth, Fine Thread, Cerulean Dye. Silk Reagent Bag: 10 slots, skill 125, pattern from the Gelkis and Magram quartermasters in Desolace. Light Leather Reagent Bag: 8 Light Leather, 1 Cured Light Hide, 3 Coarse Thread; Alliance buys the pattern from Saenorion in Darnassus (about 1 s 50 c), Horde gets it from the Durotar quest Beasts of Thunder Ridge. Warlock soul shard bags fit the slot, Hunter quivers do not. Red Linen Bag is 8 slots in Forever (skill 70, pattern 2 s). Horde Leatherworkers also have the 6-slot Kodo Hide Bag (skill 40, Thunder Bluff quest).

title: Paladin: Salvation and Blessing of Light removed
claim: Oct 31 hotfix data removes the Paladin spells Salvation, Mass Salvation, Blessing of Light, Greater Blessing of Light and Revoke, plus the talents One-Handed Weapon Specialization and Instrument of Law.
detail: Now in two independent datamines of the Oct 31 hotfix layer: wowforevertalents.com (118 Paladin changes over 70685) and playfulls.com's Paladin and Druid rework page, which lists Blessing of Light, Greater Blessing of Light, Salvation, Mass Salvation and Revoke as removed and the talents One-Handed Weapon Specialization, Instrument of Law, Voice of Truth and Improved Seal of Fury as removed (Oath of Light replaces Voice of Truth). The two sites disagree on Voice of Truth: wowforevertalents shows it as a new level-20 spell (6 s silence and interrupt immunity). Not in Blizzard's development notes. If it holds, groups lose the Paladin threat-reduction blessing, so DPS in leveling dungeons must manage threat themselves, and Holy loses the Blessing of Light healing bonus. Check the trainer and spellbook at launch.

title: Paladin: Holy Shield ranks 2-3 learned at 40 and 50
claim: Oct 31 hotfix data: Paladin Holy Shield gets a 4th rank, rank 2 moves to level 40 (was 50) and rank 3 to level 50 (was 60); damage per block is 75/110/153/221 for ranks 1-4.
detail: From playfulls.com's Oct 31 Paladin and Druid rework page: rank 1 deals 75 Holy damage per block (was 110), rank 2 at level 40 deals 110 (was 153), rank 3 at level 50 deals 153 (was 221), new rank 4 deals 221; a later Oct 31 hotfix entry says rank 4 lasts 10 s. wowforevertalents.com shows the same damage values and a 10 s cooldown but no learn levels, so the levels rest on one datamine. Holy Shield also costs 100 mana (was 150), see 20261031-paladin-oct30-talents. For Protection leveling the earlier ranks offset the lower damage per rank. Check the trainer at launch.

title: OneForAll - Forever: all-in-one companion addon
claim: OneForAll - Forever (CurseForge, about 81K downloads, updated Nov 1) puts quest and dungeon tracking, profession and recipe lookup, hunter pet info and a talent calculator in one /ofa window.
detail: CurseForge page by smoergi, file 6.0.2 for game version 1.60.1, updated Nov 1 2026, 80,999 downloads. Modules: quality-of-life options, profession and recipe lookup, hunter pet information, dungeon and quest tracking, library book tracking and a talent calculator; opened with /ofa or a minimap button. Not tested by Glide; overlaps with Glide's quest panel, so check for duplicate quest tracking.

title: No WeakAuras in Forever: use a Forever aura addon
claim: WeakAuras has no Forever version because Midnight's addon restrictions, secret values included, apply in Forever; ForeverAuras, Musca Auras, TellMeWhen or the built-in Cooldown Manager fill the gap.
detail: Blizzard said in the WoW UI Discord (reported by Wowhead on Sep 16) that Midnight's addon disarmament, secret values included, is active in Forever; WeakAuras ended development before Midnight for that reason. warcraft.wiki.gg's 1.60.1 API notes list the Midnight carryover plus Forever additions (secret FrameStrata, AuraContainer/AuraButton changes). Forever replacements on CurseForge: ForeverAuras (in development, 0.92.40 Oct 20), Musca Auras (WeakAuras 5.22 fork with a one-click HUD for all 9 classes, about 22K downloads, updated Oct 22), TellMeWhen and Cooldown Manager Centered (marked compatible by Kami Labs), and Blizzard's built-in Cooldown Manager. Combat-automation features (auto-marking, group callouts) stay blocked, so boss mods and aura packs do less than in Classic Era. A built-in damage meter is also planned. Do not install the retail/Classic WeakAuras files.

title: No TradeSkillMaster for Forever yet: use Auctionator
claim: TradeSkillMaster has no WoW Forever version (its Oct 14 release covers Retail, MoP, Classic and TBC only); Auctionator has a Forever build, so use it to scan and post at launch.
detail: Kami Labs (checked Oct 20-21) marks TSM unverified with no Forever file two weeks before launch and says not to install it; ConquestCapped's addon table (status checked Oct 29) lists TSM as no Forever version, with no word from the authors on whether one is coming. The CurseForge TSM page shows v4.14.78 (Oct 14) for Retail, MoP Classic, Classic and Classic TBC, no Forever flavor. Auctionator is marked ready/compatible by both; Auctioneer is broken (last file 2024). Matters for gold making: day-one AH flipping and pricing will run on Auctionator. Recheck after launch in case TSM ships a Forever build.

title: Addons can't read your layer from mob GUIDs
claim: Since the Oct 16 beta build, creature, pet and object GUIDs hide their server and spawn IDs, so addons can no longer tell which layer you are on by comparing mob GUIDs.
detail: warcraft.wiki.gg's Patch 1.60.1 API notes (Beta 5, 2026-10-16): the server ID and spawn ID parts of creature, vehicle, pet and game object GUIDs are obfuscated to block layer comparison; they stay stable within a session and the GUID format is otherwise unchanged. Classic layer-detection features (for example in NovaWorldBuffs-style addons) that read the zone ID from a target's GUID will not work, so layer hopping for fresh mobs or quest spawns has to rely on the official group-join layer prompt rather than an addon readout. One source (a wiki transcription of the API notes); no Blizzard statement found yet.
